rows.grounds: genitive singular of guṇin, possessor of qualities; sandhi form guṇinaḥ
passive verb indicating being carried or directed
instrumental plural of tṛṣārta, those tormented by thirst
accusative singular of ākṛti, shape or appearance

items.question: How does thirst-driven perception redirect cognition from a qualified object to mere outward form?
premises: Cognition of a qualified object can be led elsewhere.
Those afflicted by thirst are the agents of this redirection.
The redirection is oriented toward mere outward form.
items.inference: Therefore, desire-driven perception displaces apprehension of an object's qualities toward its mere appearance.
uncertainties: The exact subject implicitly carried over from the previous verse is not explicitly stated in this verse.
items.plain_english: And by those afflicted by thirst, the cognition of the qualified object is led elsewhere, toward mere outward form.
